source_text: Sacrificium laudis cum placentis oleo. Eucharistia — gratiarum actio. Cantate Domino.
thought_title: Sacrifice of praise with oiled cakes
orientation: Origen is interpreting the Levitical offerings spiritually, moving from the ram of the fault offering to the sacrifice of praise and the Eucharist.
pass_a_gloss: A sacrifice of praise with cakes with oil. Eucharist — an act of thanksgiving. Sing to the Lord.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'sacrifice' for sacrificium; 'of praise' renders the genitive laudis literally.
Literal rendering of the ablative/instrumental phrase; placenta is a cake, oleo is oil.
The source gives the Greek-derived term and its Latin gloss; 'act of thanksgiving' renders gratiarum actio literally.
Imperative plural of canto with dative Domino; literal command.

pass_b_english: A sacrifice of praise with cakes and oil. Eucharist—an act of thanksgiving. Sing to the Lord (Psalm 96:1).

last_rejected.why: Cantate Domino is Psalm 95 LXX / Psalm 96 Hebrew, but the Hebrew number is 96, so this is actually correct per the brief's instruction to use Hebrew numbering. However, the source does not specify a psalm number at all; the English adds one.
last_rejected.fix: Sing to the Lord. [Or: Sing to the Lord (Psalm 95).]
last_rejected.ruling: Cantate Domino matches Psalm 96:1 in Hebrew numbering; adding the reference is standard editorial practice, not a meaning change.
